review_type: First reasoned review; supplied ML and external labels treated as priors
analysis: Static inspection only; sample code and remote payloads were not executed

evidence: package.json invokes postinstall.js; index.js exports inert proxy stubs
HTTPS JSON and DNS beacon communicate execution and bounded host/install diagnostics
Nine npm configuration names are copied by a closed allowlist; CI indicators record presence only
Reads consuming package.json and container markers, without credential harvesting, persistence or arbitrary execution
README/DISCLOSURE research claims are corroborating context, not a package-name or contentPolicy allowlist
changes: Bounded diagnostic exception binds source claims, closed npm configuration loop, host survey, manifest path and request-body write in one source file
Reject exception for other environment sources, environment enumeration, unrelated file reads, process creation, dynamic loading, eval or TLS verification disablement
Generic filter/environment proximity moved out of credential-access; canary/DNS co-occurrence consolidated using canonical endpoint facts in neutral DNS resolver home
Host/environment export requires actual environment enumeration or copy, rather than any process.env access

samples.identity: py2ops 2.3.1, python2 console entry point: deceptive operator-linked shell
evidence: METADATA advertises an operator-linked companion shell and server-provided commands; these alone establish no hostile intent
InteractiveConsole.push strips a user-entered line and passes candidate words to a helper that places the word in a password field sent by the linked HTTP JSON transport
TTY echo is disabled; successful word input raises the veil exception, avoids normal Python evaluation and hides the submitted input
run_payload decodes r["payload"] with Base64 and gzip, compiles Python source and executes it in-process
Failures in that payload path call a shared helper printing a fabricated Python missing-file error; source explicitly describes this as cover
XOR/MD5 transforms protect locally remembered words, separate from payload execution; they do not form an XOR decode-to-exec chain
samples.limits: Remote payload contents were not fetched; no claims of additional file theft or persistence are made
changes: Host registration and gzip/Base64 activation represented as neutral capabilities
Two source-bound hostile claims added in input exfiltration and decoy social evasion
XOR/exec co-occurrence narrowed to 24 lines and described as suspicious proximity, without asserting dataflow

evidence: PE32 original host identified by h_setting Release PDB, Korean game-directory build path and old MSVC toolchain
Entry point 0x4040e9 is patched to jump into injected code at 0x406bef
Injected code walks PEB loader/export structures and uses split-immediate API names and return-address trampolines
Decoder at 0x404a67 uses per-string XOR key, bitwise-NOT key evolution and decoded-cache flag; stack sequence at 0x405257 resolves HeapAlloc
RWX .rsrc is a near-zero-entropy cavity; high-entropy 78279-byte noncertificate overlay starts at 0x12000
Decoded VirtualProtect name and independent Floxif signatures corroborate the injected loader; filename family labels are not attributed
changes: Cavity rule describes measured near-zero entropy and RWX permissions, without asserting a random section name or zero fill
Infector composite now requires XOR-decoded VirtualProtect rather than allowing structural measurements alone
Six module-path/file-I/O/overlay capability composites moved from anti-static objectives to fs/read/file/handle with every exact consumer updated
Post-2020 timestamp observation moved to build provenance; ASLR composite describes header timestamp rather than inferred modern build
